paragraphs: James River Group Holdings, Inc. owns and operates a group of specialty property and casualty insurance companies focused on underwriting small and middle market casualty risks within the U.S. excess and surplus ("E&S") lines market. For the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 84.5% of our gross written premiums and 95.9% of our net written premiums originated from the E&S lines market, which we believe puts us among the top publicly traded insurers as ranked by highest concentrations of E&S risk. Substantially all of our business is casualty insurance, and for the year ended December 31, 2025, 96.7% of our gross written premiums were derived from casualty insurance. Our objective is to generate compelling returns on tangible common equity, while limiting underwriting and investment volatility. We seek to accomplish this by earning profits from insurance underwriting and generating meaningful risk-adjusted investment returns, while efficiently managing our capital.

The Company limits its exposure to property catastrophe events to modest levels. For the year ended December 31, 2025, property insurance represented 3.3% of our gross written premiums. When we do write property insurance, we buy reinsurance to significantly mitigate our risk. We have structured our reinsurance arrangements so that our modeled net pre-tax loss from a 1/1000 year probable maximum loss ("PML") event would not exceed 2.5% of shareholders' equity on a group-wide basis, inclusive of reinstatement premiums payable and net retentions.

During the last two years, the Company has completed several strategic actions to strengthen our balance sheet and position us for long-term stability and profitable growth. In 2025, the Company concluded its leadership reorganization with new appointments on our board and across several key management positions including appointing new Presidents at both of our operating segments. We also undertook initiatives to reduce operating expenses and continued our focus on underwriting discipline and enterprise risk management. On November 7, 2025, the Company completed the Domestication of our holding company, changing the Company's incorporation from Bermuda to the U.S. The Company recognized a one-time benefit of $14.1 million related to business interest expense effective with the Domestication. The Domestication is also expected to lower the Company's effective tax rate, as holding company expenses and interest expense (previously incurred in Bermuda and ineligible for U.S. tax deduction) will receive a U.S. tax deduction in future periods, as well as bring additional operating efficiencies.

Strategic actions completed in 2024 included closing the sale of JRG Reinsurance Company Ltd. ("JRG Re") to focus our business around our U.S. insurance businesses, entering a $160.0 million combined loss portfolio transfer and adverse development cover for our Excess and Surplus Lines business, and initiating a new strategic partnership with Enstar Group Limited ("Enstar") which, in part, entailed a $12.5 million equity investment in the Company and an additional $75.0 million adverse development cover for the Excess and Surplus Lines business. Following the sale of JRG Re, our continuing operations are comprised of two operating segments, Excess and Surplus Lines and Specialty Admitted Insurance, and a third segment, Corporate and Other.

The Excess and Surplus Lines segment sells E&S commercial lines liability and property insurance in every U.S. state and the District of Columbia through James River Insurance Company ("James River Insurance") and its wholly-owned subsidiary, James River Casualty Company ("James River Casualty"). The Excess and Surplus Lines segment produced 82.1% of our gross written premiums and 95.7% of our net written premiums for the year ended December 31, 2025. James River Insurance and James River Casualty are both non-admitted carriers. Non-admitted carriers writing in the E&S market are not bound by most of the rate and form regulations imposed on standard market companies, allowing them flexibility to change the coverage terms offered and the rate charged without the time constraints and financial costs and delays associated with the filing of such changes with state regulators and seeking approval for the filings. In 2025, the average account in this segment (excluding commercial auto policies) generated annual gross written premiums of approximately $26,500, down 8.4% from the prior year. The Excess and Surplus Lines segment distributes primarily through wholesale insurance brokers and is focused on small and medium enterprise business, which we believe have been historically more profitable than other segments of the market.

The Specialty Admitted Insurance segment has admitted licenses and the authority to write excess and surplus lines insurance in 50 states and the District of Columbia through Falls Lake National Insurance Company ("Falls Lake National") and its wholly-owned subsidiaries, Stonewood Insurance Company ("Stonewood Insurance") and Falls Lake Fire and Casualty Company ("Falls Lake Fire and Casualty"). The Specialty Admitted Insurance segment produced 17.9% of our gross written premiums and 4.3% of our net written premiums for the year ended December 31, 2025. The Specialty Admitted Insurance segment primarily writes fronting business where we retain a minority share of the risk, generally less than 10%, and seek to earn fee income. When we front, we use our legal authority, financial strength rating, underwriting experience and claims infrastructure to write insurance to service clients (usually managing general agents and reinsurers) who assume the vast majority of the risk on each fronted policy. Because we retain little premium or risk in our fronted business, we can allocate less

capital per dollar of revenue to fronted policies than to policies where we retain more risk, which we believe enhances our returns on equity. The Specialty Admitted Insurance segment accepts applications for insurance from a variety of sources, including fronting and program administrators and managing general agents ("MGAs").

The Corporate and Other segment consists of the management and treasury activities of our holding companies, long-term incentive compensation for the group (including subsidiaries), public company expenses, and interest expense associated with our debt.

Our discontinued operations consists of JRG Re, which comprised the remaining operations of the former Casualty Reinsurance segment, and which, prior to the suspension of its underwriting activities in 2023, provided proportional and working layer casualty reinsurance to third parties. The sale of JRG Re, which closed on April 16, 2024, resulted in the Company's disposition of its casualty reinsurance business and related assets.
In 2025, we wrote $1,172.3 million of gross written premiums, allocated by segment and underlying market as follows:
Excess and Surplus Lines segment $ 963,035 82.1 % Specialty Admitted Insurance segment 209,284 17.9 %
Non-admitted markets $ 990,530 84.5 % Admitted markets 181,789 15.5 % $ 1,172,319 100.0 %

The A.M. Best Company ("A.M. Best") financial strength rating for our group's regulated U.S. subsidiaries is "A-" (Excellent) with a negative outlook. This rating reflects A.M. Best's opinion of our insurance subsidiaries' financial strength, operating performance and ability to meet obligations to policyholders and is not an evaluation directed towards the protection of investors. The rating for our U.S. operating insurance companies of "A-" (Excellent) is the fourth highest rating of the thirteen ratings issued by A.M. Best and is assigned to insurers that have, in A.M. Best's opinion, an excellent ability to meet their ongoing obligations to policyholders.

The financial strength ratings assigned by A.M. Best have an impact on the ability of our regulated subsidiaries to attract and retain agents and brokers and on the risk profiles of the submissions for insurance that our subsidiaries receive. We believe the "A-" (Excellent) ratings assigned to our U.S. insurance subsidiaries allow our Excess and Surplus Lines segment to actively pursue relationships with the agents and brokers identified in its marketing plans.

paragraphs: You should carefully consider the following risks, together with the cautionary statement under the caption "Special Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements" above and the other information included in this Annual Report. The risks described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks that are currently unknown to us or that we currently consider immaterial may also impair our business or materially adversely affect our financial condition or results of operations. If any of the following risks actually occurs, our business, financial condition or results of operation could be materially adversely affected.

•Reserving for losses and loss adjustment expenses is an inherently uncertain process, and our actual incurred losses and loss adjustment expenses may be greater than our loss and loss adjustment expense reserves, which could have a material adverse effect on our financial condition and results of operations.
•Our risk management is based on estimates and judgments that are subject to significant uncertainties.
•A decline in our financial strength rating may result in a reduction of new or renewal business and a default under our credit facility.
•We may not be able to retain key management and employees or recruit other qualified personnel, and as a result we may not be able to grow our business and may also be materially adversely affected.

•Adverse economic factors could result in the sale of fewer policies than expected or an increase in frequency or severity of claims and premium defaults or both, which, in turn, could affect our growth and profitability.

paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements and involves numerous risks and uncertainties, including those described under the heading "Item 1A. Risk Factors." Actual results may differ materially from those contained in any forward-looking statements. You should read this discussion and analysis together with our audited consolidated financial statements and related notes included elsewhere in this Form 10-K.

James River Group Holdings, Inc. owns and operates a group of specialty property and casualty insurance companies focused on underwriting small and middle market casualty risks within the U.S. excess and surplus ("E&S") lines market. Our objective is to generate compelling returns on tangible common equity while limiting underwriting and investment volatility. We seek to accomplish this by earning profits from insurance underwriting and generating meaningful risk-adjusted investment returns, while managing our capital.

For the year ended December 31, 2025, approximately 84.5% of our gross written premiums and 95.9% of our net written premiums originated from the U.S. E&S lines market, which we believe puts us among the top publicly traded insurers as ranked by highest concentrations of E&S risk. We also have a specialty admitted insurance business in the United States. We intend to concentrate substantially all of our underwriting in casualty insurance, and for the year ended December 31, 2025, 96.7% of our gross written premiums were derived from casualty insurance. We focus on writing business in specialty markets where our underwriters have particular expertise and where we have long-standing distribution relationships, maintaining a strong balance sheet with appropriate reserves, monitoring reinsurance recoverables carefully, managing our investment portfolio actively without taking undue risk, using technology to monitor trends in our business, responding rapidly to market opportunities and challenges, and actively managing our capital.
We report our continuing operations in three segments: Excess and Surplus Lines, Specialty Admitted Insurance, and Corporate and Other.

The Excess and Surplus Lines segment offers E&S commercial lines liability and property insurance in every U.S. state, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands through James River Insurance and its wholly-owned subsidiary, James River Casualty. James River Insurance and James River Casualty are both non-admitted carriers. Non-admitted carriers writing in the E&S market are not bound by most of the rate and form regulations imposed on standard market companies, allowing them flexibility to change the coverage terms offered and the rate charged without the time constraints and financial costs associated with the rate and form filing process. In 2025, the average account in this segment (excluding commercial auto policies) generated annual gross written premiums of approximately $26,500. The Excess and Surplus Lines segment distributes its products primarily through wholesale insurance brokers. Members of our management team have participated in this market for over twenty years and have long-standing relationships with the wholesale agents who place E&S lines accounts. The Excess and Surplus Lines segment produced 82.1% of our gross written premiums and 95.7% of our net written premiums for the year ended December 31, 2025.

The Specialty Admitted Insurance segment focuses on niche classes within the standard insurance markets through its fronting business, where we retain a minority share of the risk and seek to earn fee income by allowing other carriers and producers to use our licensure, ratings, expertise and infrastructure. Through Falls Lake National and its subsidiaries, this segment has admitted licenses and the authority to write excess and surplus lines insurance in 50 states and the District of Columbia and distributes through a variety of sources, including program administrators and MGAs. The Specialty Admitted Insurance segment produced 17.9% of our gross written premiums and 4.3% of our net written premiums for the year ended December 31, 2025.
The Corporate and Other segment consists of the management and treasury activities of our holding companies, equity compensation for the group, and interest expense associated with our debt.

Our discontinued operations include JRG Reinsurance Company Ltd. ("JRG Re"), which comprised the remaining operations of the former Casualty Reinsurance segment, and which, prior to the suspension of its underwriting activities in 2023, provided proportional and working layer casualty reinsurance to third parties. On November 8, 2023, the Company entered into a definitive agreement to sell JRG Re. The sale of JRG Re, which closed on April 16, 2024, resulted in the Company's disposition of its casualty reinsurance business and related assets.

All of the Company's U.S.-domiciled insurance subsidiaries are party to an intercompany pooling agreement that distributes the net underwriting results among the group companies based on their approximate pro-rata level of statutory capital and surplus to the total Company statutory capital and surplus. We report all segment information in this ‘‘Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations'' prior to the effects of intercompany reinsurance, consistent with the manner in which we evaluate the operating performance of our reportable segments.

The A.M. Best Company financial strength rating for our group's insurance subsidiaries is "A-" (Excellent) with a negative outlook. This rating reflects A.M. Best's evaluation of our insurance subsidiaries' financial strength, operating performance and ability to meet obligations to policyholders and is not an evaluation directed towards the protection of investors. The rating for our operating insurance companies of "A-" (Excellent) is the fourth highest rating of the thirteen ratings issued by A.M. Best and is assigned to insurers that have, in A.M. Best's opinion, an excellent ability to meet their ongoing obligations to policyholders.

The financial strength ratings assigned by A.M. Best have an impact on the ability of our insurance subsidiaries to attract and retain agents and brokers and on the risk profiles of the submissions for insurance that our subsidiaries receive. We believe the "A-" (Excellent) ratings assigned to our insurance subsidiaries allow our Excess and Surplus Lines segment to actively pursue relationships with the agents and brokers identified in its marketing plans.
We discuss certain key metrics, described below, which we believe provide useful information about our business and the operational factors underlying our financial performance.

Underwriting profit is a non-GAAP measure commonly used in the property and casualty insurance industry to evaluate underwriting performance. We believe that the disclosure of underwriting profit by individual segment and of the Company as a whole is useful to investors, analysts, rating agencies and other users of our financial information in evaluating our performance because our objective is to consistently earn underwriting profits. We evaluate the performance of our segments and allocate resources based primarily on the potential for underwriting profit. We define underwriting profit as net earned premiums and gross fee income (in specific instances when the Company is not retaining insurance risk) less losses and loss adjustment expenses on business from continuing operations not subject to retroactive reinsurance accounting and other operating expenses. Other operating expenses include the underwriting, acquisition, and insurance expenses of the operating segments and, for consolidated underwriting profit, the expenses of the Corporate and Other segment. Our definition of underwriting profit may not be comparable to that of other companies. See "Reconciliation of Non-GAAP Measures" for a reconciliation of underwriting profit to income from continuing operations before taxes and for additional information.

Loss ratio, expressed as a percentage, is the ratio of losses and loss adjustment expenses on business from continuing operations not subject to retroactive reinsurance accounting to net earned premiums. Our definition of loss ratio may not be comparable to that of other companies. See "Underwriting Performance Ratios" for a reconciliation of underwriting ratios.

paragraphs: James River Group Holdings, Inc. 擁有並經營一羣專門的財產與意外保險公司，專注於美國過失與餘額（"E&S"）市場中小規模與中規模的意外風險承保業務。截至2025年12月31日財年，約84.5%的毛寫單 premiums 以及95.9%的淨寫單 premiums 來自E&S市場，我們認為這使我們在公開交易的保險公司中，根據E&S風險的集中度排名，處於前段。我們的業務幾乎全部為意外保險，截至2025年12月31日財年，96.7%的毛寫單 premiums 來自意外保險。我們的目標是產生對實質普通股權益有吸引力的回報，同時限制承保與投資的波動性。我們透過從保險承保獲取利潤，並產生有意義的風險調整後投資回報，同時有效管理我們的資本來達成此目標。
本公司限制其對財產災害事件的敞口至相當低的水準。截至2025年12月31日財年，財產保險佔我們毛寫單 premiums 的3.3%。當我們承保財產保險時，我們會購買再保險以顯著降低我們的風險。我們已結構化再保險安排，使得我們模擬的淨稅前損失，來自1/1000年可能最大損失（"PML"）事件，不會超過股東權益的2.5%（集團層面，包括重置 premiums 支付及淨保留比例）。

在過去兩年，本公司已完成數項戰略行動以強化我們的資產負債表，並為長期穩定與獲利成長做準備。2025年，本公司完成領導層重整，包括董事會及數個關鍵管理職位的新任命，包括在兩個營運部門任命新的總經理。我們也進行了減少營運費用的行動，並持續著重於承保紀律與企業風險管理。2025年11月7日，本公司完成持有公司的內地化，將公司的註冊地從百慕達變更為美國。本公司因內地化而認列一項一次性利益為14.1百萬美元，與營業利息費用相關。內地化也預期會降低本公司的有效稅率，因為持有公司費用與利息費用（先前在百慕達產生且無法抵稅的費用）將在未來期間獲得美國稅務抵稅，同時也帶來額外的營運效率。

2024年完成的戰略行動包括出售JRG Reinsurance Company Ltd.（"JRG Re"），以專注於我們的美國保險業務，與Excess and Surplus Lines業務簽訂160.0百萬美元的合併損失組合轉讓與不利發展覆蓋，並啟動與Enstar Group Limited（"Enstar"）的新戰略合作夥伴關係，其中包含對本公司12.5百萬美元的股權投資，以及額外75.0百萬美元的不利發展覆蓋。在出售JRG Re後，我們的持續營運業務由兩個營運部門，Excess and Surplus Lines與Specialty Admitted Insurance，以及第三個部門Corporate and Other組成。

Excess and Surplus Lines部門透過James River Insurance Company（"James River Insurance"）及其全資子公司James River Casualty Company（"James River Casualty"）在美國所有州份與華盛頓特區銷售E&S商業線責任與財產保險。Excess and Surplus Lines部門在截至2025年12月31日財年產生82.1%的毛寫單 premiums 以及95.7%的淨寫單 premiums。James River Insurance與James River Casualty皆為非承認電信業者。非承認電信業者在E&S市場承保時，不受大多數標準市場公司的費率與形式規範所限制，使其能靈活變更所提供的保障條款與收費，而無需向州政府監管機構提交變更並尋求批准的時間限制與財務成本與延宕。2025年，此部門（排除商業汽車保單）的平均帳戶產生每年約26,500美元的毛寫單 premiums，較前一年下降8.4%。Excess and Surplus Lines部門主要透過 Wholesale保險經紀進行分銷，專注於中小企業業務，我們認為這些業務歷來較其他市場部門更具利潤性。

Specialty Admitted Insurance部門擁有承認牌照並具備權限在50個州份與華盛頓特區透過Falls Lake National Insurance Company（"Falls Lake National"）及其全資子公司Stonewood Insurance Company（"Stonewood Insurance"）與Falls Lake Fire and Casualty Company（"Falls Lake Fire and Casualty"）承保過失與餘額線保險。Specialty Admitted Insurance部門在截至2025年12月31日財年產生17.9%的毛寫單 premiums 以及4.3%的淨寫單 premiums。Specialty Admitted Insurance部門主要承保前線業務，我們保留少數風險，通常低於10%，並尋求獲取費用收入。當我們前線時，我們利用法律權限、財務強度評級、承保經驗與理賠基礎設施為客戶（通常是管理總代理與再保險公司）承保保險，這些客戶承擔每張前線保單的絕大多數風險。因為我們在前線業務中僅保留少量保費與風險，我們可以為每美元收入分配較少的資本至前線保單，我們認為這有助於提高我們對權益的回報。Specialty Admitted Insurance部門接受來自多種來源的保險申請，包括前線與方案管理機構與管理總代理（"MGAs"）。
Corporate and Other部門包含我們持有公司的管理與財務活動、集團（包括子公司）的長期激勵報酬、公開公司費用，以及與我們債務相關的利息費用。
Corporate and Other部門包含我們持有公司的管理與財務活動、集團（包括子公司）的長期激勵報酬、公開公司費用，以及與我們債務相關的利息費用。
本公司的 discontinued operations 為 JRG Re，其包含前 Casualty Reinsurance segment 剩餘之營運，且在 2023 年中止承保業務前，為第三方提供比例及工作層之意外再保險。JRG Re 之出售於 2024 年 4 月 16 日完成，導致本公司處分其意外再保險業務及相關資產。
2025 年，本公司寫出 1,172.3 百萬美元之 gross written premiums，依分部及基礎市場分配如下：
Excess and Surplus Lines segment $ 963,035 82.1 % Specialty Admitted Insurance segment 209,284 17.9 %
Non-admitted markets $ 990,530 84.5 % Admitted markets 181,789 15.5 % $ 1,172,319 100.0 %

A.M. Best Company ("A.M. Best") 對本公司受監管之美國子公司之財務強度評級為 "A-" (Excellent) 並為負面展望。此評級反映 A.M. Best 對本公司保險子公司財務強度、營運表現及履行對保單持有人義務能力之意見，並非針對投資者保護之評估。本公司美國營運保險公司之 "A-" (Excellent) 評級為 A.M. Best 十三種評級中之第四高評級，並賦予那些在 A.M. Best 意見中具備優秀履行對保單持有人持續義務能力之保險公司。
A.M. Best 所賦予之財務強度評級影響本公司受監管子公司吸引及保留經紀商與代理人的能力，以及子公司所收到之保險申請之風險特質。本公司認為，賦予本公司美國保險子公司之 "A-" (Excellent) 評級，使本公司 Excess and Surplus Lines 分部能積極追求其行銷計畫中所識別之經紀商與代理人之關係。

paragraphs: 以下討論與分析包含向前看的陳述，並涉及許多風險與不確定性，包括在「項目 1A. 風險因素」標題下所描述的風險。實際結果可能與任何向前看的陳述中所包含的結果有重大差異。您應將此討論與分析與我們經審計的合併財務報表及相關附註一同閱讀，這些財務報表及附註包含於本 Form 10-K 的其他部分。
James River Group Holdings, Inc. 擁有並營運一羣專門的財產與意外保險公司，專注於美國過失與剩餘（"E&S"）線市場中小企業與中型市場的意外風險承保。我們的目標是產生對實質普通股 equity 有吸引力的回報，同時限制承保與投資的波動性。我們透過從保險承保中獲利，並產生有意義的風險調整後投資回報，同時管理我們的資本來達成此目標。

截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們約 84.5% 的毛寫入保費與 95.9% 的淨寫入保費來自美國 E&S 線市場，我們認為這使我們在公開交易的保險公司中，根據 E&S 風險的集中度排名位居前列。我們也在美國擁有專門的已核准保險業務。我們意圖將我們幾乎所有的承保業務集中在意外保險，截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們 96.7% 的毛寫入保費來自意外保險。我們專注於在具備我們承保人特別專業知識與我們有長期銷售關係的專門市場中承保業務，維持強固的資產負債表與適當的準備金，謹慎監控再保險追償，積極管理我們的投資組合而不承擔過度風險，利用科技監測我們業務的趨勢，迅速回應市場的機會與挑戰，並積極管理我們的資本。
我們將持續營運分為三個應報告分部：過失與剩餘線、專門已核准保險，以及企業與其他。

過失與剩餘線分部透過 James River Insurance 及其全資子公司 James River Casualty，在美國每州、華盛頓特區、波多黎各與美國維吉尼亞羣島提供 E&S 商業線責任與財產保險。James River Insurance 及 James River Casualty 均為非已核准電信業者。在 E&S 市場中寫入保單的非已核准電信業者不受大多數標準市場公司的費率與形式規範所束縛，使其能靈活改變所提供的保障條款與收費，而不需面對與費率與形式申請程序相關的時間限制與財務成本。在 2025 年，此分部（排除商業汽車保單）的平均帳戶每年產生約 26,500 美元的毛寫入保費。過失與剩餘線分部主要透過 wholesale 保險經紀人銷售其產品。我們管理團隊的成員在這個市場已有超過二十年的經驗，並與銷售 E&S 線帳戶的 wholesale 經紀人有長期的關係。過失與剩餘線分部在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的年度中產生了 82.1% 的毛寫入保費與 95.7% 的淨寫入保費。

專門已核准保險分部透過其前承保業務專注於標準保險市場中的利基類別，我們保留風險的少數份額，並透過允許其他電信業者與經紀人使用我們的核准、評分、專業知識與基礎設施來賺取費用收入。透過 Falls Lake National 及其子公司，此分部在 50 個州與華盛頓特區擁有已核准的許可與權限，可寫入過失與剩餘線保險，並透過多種來源進行銷售，包括計畫管理機構與 MGAs。專門已核准保險分部在截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日的年度中產生了 17.9% 的毛寫入保費與 4.3% 的淨寫入保費。
企業與其他分部包含我們控股公司的管理與財務活動、集團的股票報酬，以及與我們債務相關的利息支出。
我們的已終止營運包含 JRG Reinsurance Company Ltd.（"JRG Re"），這包含前意外再保險分部的剩餘營運，且在 2023 年中止其承保活動前，為第三方提供比例與工作層意外再保險。2023 年 11 月 8 日，本公司與 JRG Re 籤訂了最終協議，出售 JRG Re，該交易於 2024 年 4 月 16 日完成，使本公司放棄其意外再保險業務與相關資產。
本公司所有美國設立的保險子公司均為一項內部合併協議之參與方，該協議根據各子公司約當比例之法定資本及準備金與總公司法定資本及準備金之關係，將淨承保結果分配給各集團公司。我們在本「第 7 項 管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」中報告所有分部資訊，並未扣除內部再保險之影響，與我們評估應報告分部營運表現之方式一致。

A.M. Best 公司對我們集團保險子公司之財務強度評級為「A-」（優秀），展望為負面。此評級反映 A.M. Best 公司對我們保險子公司財務強度、營運表現及履行對保單持有人義務之能力之評估，並非針對投資者保護之評估。我們營運保險公司之「A-」（優秀）評級為 A.M. Best 公司十三種評級中之第四高評級，並賦予那些在 A.M. Best 公司觀點中具備優秀能力履行對保單持有人持續義務之保險公司。
A.M. Best 公司所賦予之財務強度評級會影響我們保險子公司吸引及留住經紀人與代理人的能力，以及我們子公司所接獲之保險申請之風險特質。我們認為賦予我們保險子公司之「A-」（優秀）評級，使我們過失與超額線業務分部能積極追求其行銷計畫中所識別之經紀人與代理人之關係。
我們討論下列某些關鍵指標，我們認為這些指標能提供有關我們業務及我們財務表現背後營運因素之有用資訊。

承保獲利為一非 GAAP 指標，常被用於財產與意外保險業評估承保表現。我們認為揭露各個分部及本公司整體之承保獲利，對投資者、分析師、評級機構及其他使用我們財務資訊之人士評估我們表現是有用的，因為我們的目標是持續獲取承保獲利。我們評估各個分部之表現並根據各分部潛在承保獲利之能力主要分配資源。我們定義承保獲利為淨收取保費及總費用收入（在特定情況下本公司未保留保險風險時），減去來自持續營運之業務之損失及損失調整費用，以及其他營運費用。其他營運費用包括營運分部之承保、獲客及保險費用，以及對於合併承保獲利，則包括企業及其他分部之費用。我們對承保獲利之定義可能與其他公司不具可比性。請參閱「非 GAAP 指標之調整」以取得承保獲利與持續營運之稅前營業收入之調整資訊，以及更多資訊。
損失比率以百分比表示，為來自持續營運之業務之損失及損失調整費用與淨收取保費之比率。我們對損失比率之定義可能與其他公司不具可比性。請參閱「承保表現比率」以取得承保比率之調整資訊。

headings: 與我們業務及產業相關之風險
與本公司普通股之持有相關之風險
本公司之風險管理係基於估計與判斷，而這些估計與判斷會受到重大不確定性之影響。
若本公司之財務強度評級下降，可能會導致新業務或續約業務減少，並導致本公司在信貸融資協議下發生違約。
若本公司無法留住關鍵管理階層與員工，或無法招募其他合格之人力，本公司可能會受到重大不利影響。
本公司可能無法以合理價格或提供足夠保障之條款取得再保險之保障。
本公司面臨因再保險對手、保險公司及與前客戶所訂立之賠償協議而產生之信用風險。
若我們所採用之損失限制或除外責任失效，或因其他聲請或保險範圍問題產生變化，可能對本公司之財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。
新興聲請及保險範圍問題對本公司業務之影響尚屬不確定。
本公司投資組合面臨顯著之市場及信用風險，可能導致對本公司財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。
本公司可能面臨額外之政府或市場監管，可能對本公司業務造成重大不利影響。
paragraphs: 您應謹慎考慮下列風險，並與上文標題為「特別提醒有關未來展望陳述」的警示聲明及本年度報告中包含的其他資訊一併考量。下列所描述的風險並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。目前我們尚未知悉或目前認為不重要的其他風險，也可能會影響我們的業務或對我們的財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。若任何上述風險實際發生，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大不利影響。
•對於損失及損失調整費用的提列是一項本質上不確定的程序，我們實際發生的損失及損失調整費用可能高於我們所提列的損失及損失調整費用準備金，這可能會對我們的財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
•我們的風險管理是基於估計與判斷，而這些估計與判斷會受到重大不確定性影響。
•我們的財務強度評級下降可能會導致新業務或續保業務減少，並導致我們的信貸協議出現違約。
•我們可能無法留住關鍵管理階層與員工，或招募其他合格人才，因此我們可能無法擴張業務，同時也可能對我們造成重大不利影響。
•不利的總體經濟因素可能會導致銷售的保單數量低於預期，或導致聲請數量或聲請金額增加，或同時出現上述情況，這可能會影響我們的成長與獲利能力。
